title: Iridium spike in a 12,900-year-old Greenland ice core layer
summary: Randall Carlson tells of Iridium spike in a 12,900-year-old Greenland ice core layer, about 12,900 years ago at Greenland, and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: excavate a core ice core from Greenland and then you discover that there is a 12,900year layer of glacial ice that has a spike of aridium in it hundreds of times greater than the background.
they've got core samples that show a large amount of aridium.
tellings.difference: Told second hand by Joe Rogan, who does not say Greenland, give the 12,900-year date or say how large the spike is.
tellings.link_reason: Both say core samples from the Younger Dryas boundary show a large spike of iridium.

as_told.title: Younger Dryas impact and core-sample iridium

plain: A researcher named Randall Carlson, speaking with a podcast host named Jesse Michels, says that scientists drilled an ice core in Greenland, which is a long cylinder of ancient ice pulled up from deep in the ice sheet. According to Carlson, the layer that formed about 12,900 years ago holds a spike of iridium, a rare metal, hundreds of times above normal levels. Another podcast host, Joe Rogan, repeats a shorter version second hand: he says only that core samples show a large amount of iridium, and gives no place, date or size. People tell it because, if true, it would point to some sudden catastrophe hitting the Earth at that moment.
